inputs.text: Health workers protesting the proposed reform bills at Unity Fountain in Maitama on Thursday are defending more than their own interests: they are warning that decisions made without frontline voices can worsen care and working conditions. The National Assembly must not dismiss their concerns as “union interests” or mistake public pressure for a reason to shut down debate. When a health system is already strained, reforms imposed from above risk leaving workers and patients—especially people with the fewest resources—to bear the cost. Listen to those doing the work, and judge the bills by whether they make care fairer and stronger for everyone.
